Name of the Surah

• It is called "an-Nasr" (The Help/Victory), because it opens with mention of Allah's victory granted to the Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers in the conquest of Makkah.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• The promise of a great victory from Allah through the conquest of Makkah, the good news of many people entering Islam, the command to the Prophet (ﷺ) to give thanks for this blessing by glorifying Allah and frequently seeking His forgiveness, the indication of the perfection of this religion, and the nearness of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) passing to the Hereafter.

[The Tafsir]

If victory over the disbelievers of Quraysh has been completed for you, O Messenger, and the conquest of "Makkah" has been accomplished for you.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 110, verse 2:

And I saw many people entering into Islam in groups, group after group.

If that happens, then prepare yourself for the meeting with your Lord by glorifying Him with His praise abundantly and by asking Him for forgiveness abundantly. Indeed, He is ever accepting of repentance from those who glorify Him and seek His forgiveness; He turns to them in mercy, has compassion on them, and accepts their repentance.
